units.translation: Now Athena turns to the departing chorus, to whom she now wishes to assign seats along with her citizens. It is striking that here the ⟦1⟧ are mentioned as already present (⟦2⟧), and likewise the sacrificial victims as present (1006). However, the goddess can arrange whatever she wishes without saying so and without it being noticed; whether, moreover, reference is made to something already visible is questionable, cf. on 1025 f. ⟦3⟧ also ⟦4⟧. — 1007

⟦1⟧: see on 786; for what follows, in which what is prayed for from chthonic deities in general is stated, cf. ⟦2⟧ (⟦3⟧) ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧. The genitive ⟦6⟧, which is difficult to construe, Paley has emended to the dative; then ⟦7⟧ belongs together (⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧. 868 with reference to the single actual battle; different here, where one will compare 974 f.). In 1010 the Areopagites are undoubtedly addressed, as in 949; since Athena herself has declared that she will lead, it must read ⟦10⟧.
to send good things to you and to your child from beneath the earth into the light
but the opposite of these, to be allotted to the darkness beneath the earth

⟦1⟧ 775. 883; the legendary ⟦2⟧, as eponymous hero of the ancient ⟦3⟧, who in turn are named from the ⟦4⟧, appears here for the first time. ⟦5⟧ says that the Athenians in Pelasgian times were Pelasgians, under the name ⟦6⟧; the ⟦7⟧ occurs in Aristoph. ⟦8⟧. 75 (exclamation ⟦9⟧. ⟦10⟧.), Lysistr. 480 ⟦11⟧ (the Acropolis), ⟦12⟧. 123 ⟦13⟧ (Athens), and is said (Schol. Ach.) to have occurred also in Aeschylus and Sophocles. With the last words, likewise addressed to the representatives of the citizenry, Athena recalls 985 (⟦14⟧); on the meaning see on 975. Chorus antistr. ⟦15⟧, 1014–1020, another farewell. The ⟦16⟧' ⟦17⟧ must refer to 996, and likewise the † ⟦18⟧, in which ⟦19⟧. may lie (Weil; with a nevertheless striking plural), or ⟦20⟧ (Wieseler); further afield are ⟦21⟧ (Hermann, after ⟦22⟧ ⟦23⟧) and ⟦24⟧ (Ddf.). The simplex ⟦25⟧ stands at ⟦26⟧. For the sense, ⟦27⟧- seems more essential than ⟦28⟧, and thus I have adopted ⟦29⟧. ⟦30⟧ instead of ⟦31⟧ not only removes the rarer construction ⟦32⟧ (⟦33⟧, Phoen. 1321, cf. ⟦34⟧ ⟦35⟧⟦36⟧), but it also strengthens the sense, since ⟦37⟧ is the same as ⟦38⟧. Aeschylus wrote E⟦39⟧, which can be this or that. Cf. ⟦40⟧ 645 and elsewhere.
